headings.title: Offense of animal neglect defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of animal neglect when a custodian fails to provide adequate care or knowingly abandons an animal without care provisions.

headings.title: Penalty classification for animal neglect
headings.reviewNote: Classifies animal neglect as a class C misdemeanor, elevated to a class B misdemeanor if previously found guilty under this section or an equivalent out-of-jurisdiction offense.

headings.title: Discretionary waiver of fines and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to waive first-offense fines upon proof of permanent remedies, prohibits waiving maintenance costs, and exempts sections 578.007 and chapter 272.

headings.title: Court-ordered restitution for care and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the court to order restitution for animal care, carcass disposal, organic debris cleanup, and public health risk mitigation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.009 covering animal neglect elements, misdemeanor penalty grading, discretionary first-offense fine waivers and exceptions, and discretionary care and cleanup restitution (L. 1983 S.B. 211 § 3 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of animal trespass defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines animal trespass when an owner or custodian knowingly fails to provide adequate control of an animal for twelve hours or more.

headings.title: Penalty classification and fine waiver conditions
headings.reviewNote: Classifies animal trespass as an infraction (fine up to $200) for a first conviction and a class C misdemeanor (imprisonment and/or fine up to $500) for subsequent convictions, permits first-offense fine waivers upon permanent remedy while barring waiver of care costs, and excludes section 578.007 and sections 272.010 to 272.370.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.011 covering animal trespass elements, infraction and class C misdemeanor grading, first-offense fine waivers, and exemptions (L. 2013 S.B. 9; effective 10-11-13 after veto override).

headings.title: Offense of animal abuse defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines animal abuse as intentionally killing an animal without authorization, purposely inflicting injury or suffering, or knowingly failing to provide care resulting in substantial harm.

headings.title: Penalty classification and felony enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies animal abuse as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to a class E felony for prior offenses or torture and mutilation consciously inflicted while alive.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.012 covering animal abuse elements, class A misdemeanor grading, and class E felony enhancements for repeat offenses or torture/mutilation (L. 1983 S.B. 211 § 4 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17; source annotation notes State v. Price).

headings.title: Mandatory submission of farm animal recordings
headings.reviewNote: Requires farm animal professionals who record suspected animal abuse or neglect to submit recordings to law enforcement within twenty-four hours.

headings.title: Prohibition against editing or manipulating recordings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits splicing, editing, or manipulating any videotape or digital recording in any way prior to submission under subsection 1.

headings.title: Penalty for intentional violation of section
headings.reviewNote: Classifies an intentional violation of any provision of this section as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.013 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2 and corrected subsection 3 penalty from class B to class A misdemeanor) covering 24-hour recording submission duty, ban on editing or manipulating recordings, and class A misdemeanor penalty (L. 2012 S.B. 631).

headings.title: Impoundment and disposition of neglected or abused animals
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public health, law enforcement, or animal control officials to impound animals showing evidence of neglect or abuse off the owner's property, prescribing five-business-day owner notice, ten- or five-business-day hold periods, adoption, or humane killing.

headings.title: Owner liability for costs, lien, and excess proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Holds the owner or custodian liable for reasonable care and maintenance costs, grants a lien with authority to place for adoption or humanely kill if unpaid within ten days after demand, and directs excess adoption proceeds to the owner.

headings.title: Recovery of value for unwarranted killing
headings.reviewNote: Entitles the owner or custodian of an animal killed under this section to recover its actual value up to six hundred dollars upon showing that the killing was unwarranted.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.016 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 and 3 and refined subsection 1) covering off-property impoundment and hold periods, owner cost liability and lien, and up to $600 recovery for unwarranted killing (L. 1983 S.B. 211 § 6).

headings.title: Warrant application and entry on private property
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public health or law enforcement officials to obtain a probable-cause warrant to enter private property to inspect, care for, or impound neglected or abused animals, requiring a 30-day disposition hearing, proper care placement, licensed-veterinarian humane killing determinations, and immunity for necessary property damage.

headings.title: Bond or security to prevent disposition and notice
headings.reviewNote: Permits the owner, custodian, or interested person to prevent disposition by posting bond or security covering at least thirty days of care and keeping, allows humane disposition after the bonded period absent a court order with further bond, and requires posting or delivering notice of this section.

headings.title: Bar on damages recovery for humanely killed animals
headings.reviewNote: Bars the owner or custodian from recovering damages or actual value for an animal humanely killed under this section if a licensed veterinarian found it diseased or disabled or if the owner or custodian failed to post bond or security after notice of impoundment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.018 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 and 3 and tightened subsection 1) covering entry warrants and disposition hearings, 30-day care bonds and notice, and bar on damages recovery for humanely killed animals (L. 1983 S.B. 211 § 7 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17; annotation notes State ex rel. Zobel v. Burrell).

headings.title: Offense of keeping dangerous wild animals
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of keeping listed dangerous wild animals or reptiles outside specified exempt facilities (such as zoological parks, circuses, research institutions, veterinary hospitals, or refuges) without registering them with the local law enforcement agency in the county.

headings.title: Penalty classification for keeping dangerous wild animals
headings.reviewNote: Classifies the offense of keeping a dangerous wild animal as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.023 (tightened subsection 1 note and subsection 2 title) covering keeping dangerous wild animals without local law enforcement registration and class C misdemeanor penalty (L. 1983 S.B. 211 § 9 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of keeping a dangerous dog defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines keeping a dangerous dog as owning or possessing a dog that previously bit a person or domestic animal without provocation and subsequently bites any person.

headings.title: Penalty classifications and felony enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies keeping a dangerous dog as a class B misdemeanor, elevated to a class A misdemeanor for serious injury, a class E felony for serious injury with a prior serious-injury attack, and a class D felony for death of any person.

headings.title: Immediate seizure, impoundment, and destruction of dog
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate seizure by an animal control authority or county sheriff, ten-business-day impoundment after written notification to the owner or possessor, and destruction thereafter for repeat biting dogs or dogs causing serious injury or death.

headings.title: Circuit court appeal and disposition hearing
headings.reviewNote: Permits the owner or possessor to appeal impoundment and destruction to the circuit court with notice to the seizing authority, stays destruction pending a thirty-day disposition hearing, and authorizes ordering payment of care and keeping costs.

headings.title: Exemption when victim engaged in criminal activity
headings.reviewNote: Exempts the owner or possessor from criminal guilt and civil liability and bars destruction of the dog when the bitten person was engaged in or attempting criminal activity, excluding simple trespass under section 569.150 or trespass by a person under twelve under section 569.140.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 578.024 (rewrote shifted subsections 2 through 5 and corrected subsection 1 note) covering dangerous dog offense, penalty tiers, immediate seizure and destruction, circuit court appeal and 30-day hearing, and criminal-activity exemption (L. 2009 H.B. 62, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of dogfighting defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines dogfighting as owning, possessing, keeping, or training a dog with intent to fight, causing dogs to fight or injure each other for amusement or gain, or permitting or aiding and abetting such acts on controlled premises.

headings.title: Felony classification for dogfighting offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies the offense of dogfighting as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.025 covering dogfighting offense elements and class E felony classification (L. 1984 H.B. 1210 § 1, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Spectating dogfighting offense defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines spectating dogfighting as knowingly being present as a spectator with intent to be present at dogfighting preparations, exhibitions, or fighting/injuring under section 578.025(1)(2).

headings.title: Penalty classification for spectating dogfighting
headings.reviewNote: Designates spectating dogfighting as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Exemptions for livestock management, hunting, and training
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not prohibit using dogs in livestock management or hunting, or training dogs and using training equipment for any lawful purpose.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.026 (rewrote fabricated subsection 3) covering spectating dogfighting or preparations, class A misdemeanor penalty, and exemptions for livestock management, hunting, and lawful training (L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Prohibited pursuit of propelled live animals
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of tying, attaching, or fastening any live animal to a power-propelled machine or device to cause pursuit by a dog or dogs.

headings.title: Penalty classification for propelled live animal pursuit
headings.reviewNote: Classifies causing a dog to pursue a live animal propelled by a device as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.027 covering tying or fastening a live animal to a propelled device for dog pursuit and class A misdemeanor penalty (L. 1984 H.B. 1210 § 3, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Unlawful removal of electronic dog collars
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful removal of an electronic or radio transmitting collar from a dog without owner permission with intent to prevent or hinder the owner from locating the dog.

headings.title: Penalty classification and restitution orders
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful collar removal as a class A misdemeanor, mandates restitution for the actual value of any dog lost or killed as a result, and permits restitution for lost breeding revenues.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.028 (corrected subsection 1 and 2 notes) covering unauthorized removal of electronic or radio dog collars with intent to hinder location, class A misdemeanor penalty, mandatory dog-value restitution, and discretionary breeding-revenue restitution (L. 2009 H.B. 62, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of knowingly releasing an animal
headings.reviewNote: Defines knowingly releasing an animal as intentionally releasing, without owner or custodian consent, an animal lawfully confined for companionship, protection, recreation, exhibition, or educational purposes.

headings.title: Definition of animal for this section
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'animal' for purposes of this section as every living creature, domesticated or wild, excluding Homo sapiens.

headings.title: Public servant official duty exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts public servants acting in the ordinary course of their official duties from animal release offenses.

headings.title: Penalty classification and repeat offender enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unauthorized animal release as a class B misdemeanor, elevated to a class E felony for repeat offenders.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.029 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2) covering unauthorized intentional release of confined animals, definition of animal, public servant exemption, and class B misdemeanor / class E felony repeat penalties (L. 2001 S.B. 462, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Search warrant authority for animal offenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state highway patrol officers and peace officers to apply for and serve search warrants to enforce animal fighting laws.

headings.title: Seizure, custody, and forfeiture procedures
headings.reviewNote: Governs the lawful seizure, affidavit filing, judicial custody, and forfeiture or return of animals and fighting paraphernalia upon arrest.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.030 covering state highway patrol and law enforcement search warrant authority under sections 578.025 to 578.050 and seizure, custody, and forfeiture procedures for section 578.025 arrests (L. 1984 H.B. 1210 §§ 2, 4, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Bullbaiting and cockfighting offense defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits keeping premises, aiding, or permitting premises to be used for baiting or fighting bulls, bears, cocks, or other non-canine animals.

headings.title: Penalty classification for bullbaiting or cockfighting
headings.reviewNote: Classifies bullbaiting or cockfighting as a class A misdemeanor (noting judicial vagueness challenge in State v. Young).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.050 covering bullbaiting and cockfighting elements and class A misdemeanor grading (RSMo 1939 § 4789 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17; source annotation notes 1985 State v. Young unconstitutional vagueness holding).

headings.title: Offense of flag desecration defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits purposefully and publicly defacing, trampling upon, or desecrating the United States or Missouri state flag.

headings.title: Penalty classification for flag desecration
headings.reviewNote: Designates flag desecration as a class A misdemeanor (noting Snider v. City of Cape Girardeau First Amendment ruling).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.095 covering flag desecration elements and class A misdemeanor grading (L. 1980 H.B. 965 § 1, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17; source annotation notes 2014 Snider v. City of Cape Girardeau First Amendment overbreadth holding).

headings.title: Prohibited retail sales on Sunday and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits Sunday retail sales of designated goods including motor vehicles, clothing, appliances, and hardware, imposing misdemeanor fines and jail.

headings.title: Separate offense for each transaction
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that each separate retail sale or offer to sell on Sunday constitutes a distinct offense.

headings.title: Five-day limitation period for charging violations
headings.reviewNote: Requires criminal information charging Sunday sales violations to be filed within five days of the alleged offense.

headings.title: Common nuisance declaration for unlawful operations
headings.reviewNote: Declares any business operating in violation of Sunday sales restrictions to be a public and common nuisance.

headings.title: County exemption election in large metropolitan areas
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes counties containing all or part of a city over 400,000 population to exempt themselves from Sunday sales bans by local voter referendum.

headings.title: County exemption by governing body order or ordinance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any county governing body to exempt the county from this section by order or ordinance after a public hearing preceded by at least three newspaper notices, effective upon filing and certification with the secretary of state and revisor of statutes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 578.100 (rewrote inaccurate subsection 6) covering Sunday retail sales bans and penalties, separate offenses, five-day charging limit, common nuisance status, voter exemption in counties with a city over 400,000, and county governing-body exemption by order or ordinance (L. 1963 p. 685 § 1 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 157 & 29 merged with S.B. 180; Revisor's Note lists Jackson, Clay, and Platte counties).

headings.title: City ordinance exemption near convention center or auditorium
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a city not within a county to exempt by ordinance defined areas within 2,500 yards of a city-owned convention center or municipal auditorium from section 578.100, excluding automobile sales, upon filing with the secretary of state and revisor of statutes.

headings.title: Prohibition on lease provisions requiring Sunday opening
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits lessors of retail structures in an exempted area from including any lease or contract provision that directly or indirectly requires the lessee to open on Sundays after the exemption takes effect.

headings.title: Protection of preexisting leases from Sunday opening
headings.reviewNote: Provides that preexisting retail leases in effect prior to an exemption shall not be interpreted to require Sunday opening if the lessee was not required to open on Sundays when signing.

headings.title: Severability of unconstitutional provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that remaining portions of this section remain valid if any portion is held unconstitutional unless essentially and inseparably connected with the invalid provision.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.106 (rewrote all 4 subsections to match source text) covering city-not-within-a-county ordinance exemption within 2,500 yards of a convention center or auditorium (excluding automobile sales), prospective and preexisting retail lease protections against mandatory Sunday opening, and severability (L. 1983 S.B. 391; Revisor's Note records Oct. 6, 1983 City of St. Louis filing).

headings.title: Definitions of area and county
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'area' as cities not within a county and specified adjoining first-class counties, and 'county' as any Missouri county not within such an area.

headings.title: Voter authorization for county or area exemption
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any other county or area to exempt itself from section 578.100 by voter approval, requiring simultaneous voting across every city and county within an area and a majority of total area votes cast.

headings.title: Referendum petition, ballot language, and filing certification
headings.reviewNote: Establishes governing-body or eight-percent voter petition submission, ballot language, majority vote effect, and required filing and certification with the secretary of state and revisor of statutes before exemption takes effect.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.110 (rewrote all 3 shifted subsections) covering definitions of area and county, voter authorization for county or area exemption, and referendum petition, ballot language, and filing certification (L. 1979 H.B. 56 § 1; Revisor's Note table lists exempt counties; annotation notes 1980 Gramex Corp. v. Von Romer holding 'area' method unconstitutional and severable).

headings.title: Prohibition against Sunday motor vehicle sales
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensed motor vehicle dealers, distributors, or manufacturers from operating on Sunday to buy, sell, barter, or exchange motor vehicles, with exceptions for manufactured housing, RVs, motorcycles, powersports and electric bicycles, washing/towing/repairing, fuel/parts, and qualifying multi-dealer shows.

headings.title: Dealer association closing agreements antitrust exemption
headings.reviewNote: Protects dealer associations encouraging Sunday dealership closures from state antitrust and restraint of trade liability.

headings.title: Penalty classification for unlawful Sunday vehicle sales
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violating Sunday motor vehicle sales restrictions as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.120 (corrected history citation and expanded subsection 1 note) covering Sunday motor vehicle sales ban and exceptions, dealer association antitrust exemption, and class C misdemeanor penalty (L. 1985 H.B. 154 §§ 1, 2 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 176).

headings.title: Legislative intent recognizing right to hunt, fish, and trap
headings.reviewNote: Declares the general assembly's intent to recognize that all persons shall have the right to hunt, fish, and trap in Missouri in accordance with law and conservation commission rules under Article IV of the Missouri Constitution.

headings.title: Offense of interference in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines interference with hunting, fishing, or trapping in the first degree as intentionally interfering with the lawful taking of wildlife by another.

headings.title: Harassing, driving, or disturbing wildlife as violation
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that intentionally harassing, driving, or disturbing any game animal or fish for the purpose of disrupting lawful hunting, fishing, or trapping violates this section.

headings.title: Penalty classification for first-degree interference
headings.reviewNote: Classifies interference with lawful hunting, fishing, or trapping in the first degree as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.151 (rewrote all 4 shifted/fabricated subsections) covering legislative intent recognizing hunting/fishing/trapping rights, first-degree interference elements, wildlife harassment violation, and class A misdemeanor penalty (L. 1988 S.B. 434 & 435 § 1 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of hunter interference in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines interference with hunting, fishing, or trapping in the second degree as entering or remaining in an area where lawful hunting, fishing, or trapping may occur with intent to interfere with the lawful taking of wildlife.

headings.title: Penalty classification for second-degree hunter interference
headings.reviewNote: Designates interference with lawful hunting, fishing, or trapping in the second degree as a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.152 (corrected fabricated subsection 1 note) covering entering or remaining in a hunting, fishing, or trapping area with intent to interfere and class B misdemeanor penalty (L. 1988 S.B. 434 & 435 § 2 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Order to desist and class A misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a chapter 590 peace officer who reasonably believes a person violated section 578.151 or 578.152 to order the person to desist, and classifies failure to obey such order as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Enforcement and arrest authority of officers and agents
headings.reviewNote: Directs that any law enforcement officer shall, and any conservation commission agent may, enforce sections 578.151, 578.152, and this section and arrest violators.

headings.title: Exemption for lawful landowner or possessor activity
headings.reviewNote: Excludes any lawful activity by the landowner or persons in lawful possession of the land from conduct declared unlawful under sections 578.151 and 578.152.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.153 (rewrote all 3 shifted/wrong subsections) covering peace officer desist orders and class A misdemeanor penalty, law enforcement and conservation agent enforcement authority, and lawful landowner/possessor exemption (L. 1988 S.B. 434 & 435 § 3 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of interference with livestock transportation
headings.reviewNote: Defines interference with livestock transportation as knowingly stopping, boarding, or obstructing a motor vehicle transporting livestock, provoking or disturbing confined livestock, or placing substances affecting livestock marketability, health, or shipping.

headings.title: Felony penalties for livestock transportation interference
headings.reviewNote: Classifies interference with the transportation of livestock as a class E felony for a first offense and a class C felony for any second or subsequent offense.

headings.title: Affirmative defense of consent
headings.reviewNote: Allows a defendant to assert an affirmative defense of consent, proved by a preponderance of the evidence, from a person with real or apparent authority to transport, possess, or control the livestock or the livestock owner.

headings.title: Exemption for law enforcement and agriculture department
headings.reviewNote: Exempts any enforcement action or services provided by a law enforcement officer or agency or a department of agriculture employee or agent acting under section 267.645.

headings.title: Definitions of livestock and motor vehicle
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'livestock' by reference to section 265.300 and 'motor vehicle' as any self-propelled vehicle not operated exclusively on tracks and attached items, excluding farm tractors and electric bicycles.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 578.156 (rewrote subsections 2–5 and corrected subsection 1 note and enactment citation) covering livestock transport interference elements, class E / class C felony penalties, consent affirmative defense, law enforcement and agriculture department exemption, and definitions (L. 2023 S.B. 186).

headings.title: Offense of baiting or fighting animals defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits baiting, fighting, or inciting combat between animals, possessing baiting paraphernalia, or attending such exhibitions.

headings.title: Felony classification for animal fighting and baiting
headings.reviewNote: Designates baiting or fighting animals as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.173 covering animal baiting and fighting elements and class E felony penalty (Proposition A § B, Nov. 3, 1998, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17; annotation notes United Gamefowl Breeders Ass'n. of Missouri v. Nixon).

headings.title: Offense of bear wrestling defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits engaging in wrestling matches with bears, promoting or staging bear wrestling exhibitions, or surgically altering bears for wrestling.

headings.title: Penalty classification for bear wrestling
headings.reviewNote: Classifies the offense of bear wrestling as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.176 (corrected subsection 2 penalty from class E felony to class A misdemeanor) covering bear wrestling elements and class A misdemeanor classification (Proposition A § C, Nov. 3, 1998, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17; annotation notes United Gamefowl Breeders Ass'n. of Missouri v. Nixon).

headings.title: Infraction of medical deception for failing to report gunshot wounds
headings.reviewNote: Defines the infraction of medical deception when a chapter 334 or 335 licensee treating a gunshot wound knowingly fails to immediately report the patient's identity or description, wound nature, and treatment circumstances to local law enforcement.

headings.title: Civil immunity and physician-patient privilege exception
headings.reviewNote: Grants good-faith civil immunity for reporting gunshot wounds and participating in related judicial proceedings, and provides that the physician-patient privilege under section 491.060(5) does not bar reporting or admissible testimony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.350 (rewrote both fabricated subsections) covering infraction of medical deception for failing to report gunshot wounds and good-faith civil immunity with physician-patient privilege exception (L. 1985 S.B. 54 § 1, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Short title as Danny's Law
headings.reviewNote: Designates this section as 'Danny's Law'.

headings.title: Offense of hazing defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of hazing involving willful acts on or off college or university campuses that recklessly endanger physical or mental health or safety or require criminal law violations for organizational initiation, admission, or continued membership.

headings.title: Mandatory college and university anti-hazing policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires public and private colleges and universities in Missouri to adopt a written policy prohibiting hazing by any organization operating under the sanction of the institution.

headings.title: No new private cause of action against institutions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section shall be interpreted as creating a new private cause of action against any educational institution.

headings.title: Consent not a defense and inapplicability of section 565.010
headings.reviewNote: Provides that consent is not a defense to hazing and that section 565.010 does not apply to hazing cases or homicide cases arising out of hazing activity.

headings.title: Penalty classification for hazing
headings.reviewNote: Classifies hazing as a class A misdemeanor, or a class D felony if the act creates a substantial risk to the life of the student or prospective, current, or former member.

headings.title: Defense for first caller seeking immediate medical assistance
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a person is not guilty of hazing upon establishing all four statutory elements: presence at the event, being the first to call 911 or campus security, providing name, address, and issue description, and remaining at the scene to cooperate with responders.

headings.title: Immunity from prosecution for rendering aid
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from prosecution under this section, notwithstanding subsection 7, to a person who establishes rendering good-faith aid such as CPR, airway clearance, or defibrillator use before responders arrive.

headings.title: Definition of former member
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'former member' as a person no longer affiliated with the local chapter of an institutionally sanctioned organization who may remain affiliated with its national chapter.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsection headings for 578.365 (rewrote all 9 shifted/fabricated subsections and corrected enactment history) covering Danny's Law short title, hazing elements, institutional policies, no new private cause of action, consent bar, class A misdemeanor / class D felony penalties, first-caller defense, aid-rendering immunity, and former member definition (L. 1987 H.B. 126 § 3 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 43 merged with S.B. 160).

headings.title: Offense of sports bribery in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines first-degree sports bribery as giving, promising, or offering any benefit to a participant or prospective participant with the purpose to influence them to lose, try to lose, or limit the margin of victory.

headings.title: Felony classification for first-degree sports bribery
headings.reviewNote: Designates sports bribery in the first degree as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.398 (tightened subsection 1 note) covering first-degree sports bribery elements and class D felony classification (L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of sports bribery in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines second-degree sports bribery as a participant or prospective participant accepting, attempting to obtain, or soliciting any benefit in exchange for losing, trying to lose, or limiting the margin of victory.

headings.title: Penalty classification for second-degree sports bribery
headings.reviewNote: Classifies sports bribery in the second degree as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.399 (corrected subsection 2 penalty from class E felony to class A misdemeanor and tightened subsection 1 note) covering second-degree sports bribery elements and class A misdemeanor classification (L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Short title of act
headings.reviewNote: Designates this section as 'The Animal Research and Production Facilities Protection Act'.

headings.title: Definitions of animal and animal facility
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'animal' (excluding Homo sapiens) and 'animal facility' (including scientific research, agricultural production, veterinary medicine, pet food, representing organizations, personnel, offices, vehicles, and premises).

headings.title: Prohibited acts against animal research and production facilities
headings.reviewNote: Defines six prohibited acts against animal facilities, including unauthorized release or harm to animals, property damage or theft, access by false pretenses, unauthorized interference with records or data, and entering or remaining with unlawful intent (source footnote notes subsection 3 was transferred from former section 578.407 in 2014).

headings.title: Penalty classifications based on loss or damage
headings.reviewNote: Classifies prohibited acts against animal facilities as a class A misdemeanor, or a class E, D, C, or B felony for loss or damage of at least $750, $1,000, $25,000, or $75,000, respectively.

headings.title: Conspiracy to violate section
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any person who intentionally agrees with another to violate this section and commits an act in furtherance to the same penalty class provided in subsection 4.

headings.title: Court hearing to determine value of loss or damage
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to conduct a hearing to determine the reasonable replacement cost of damaged, destroyed, or lost materials, data, equipment, animals, and records, plus lost production funds and costs of repeating disrupted experimentation.

headings.title: Joint and several liability for restitution orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to order any person found guilty under this section to make restitution, jointly and severally, to the owner, operator, or both for the full reasonable cost determined under subsection 6.

headings.title: Private civil cause of action for damages
headings.reviewNote: Creates a private right of action authorizing facility owners to recover actual damages, punitive damages, and attorney fees.

headings.title: Injunctive relief and permanent court orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes courts to issue temporary restraining orders and permanent injunctions barring unlawful facility interference.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of agriculture rulemaking and investigative enforcement with assistance from the attorney general, highway patrol, and law enforcement, subject to chapter 536 and a nonseverability clause with a January 1, 2017 cutoff.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsection headings for 578.405 (rewrote shifted subsections 1 through 6 and tightened subsection 7 and 10 notes) covering short title, definitions, prohibited acts (transferred from former 578.407), loss-based misdemeanor/felony tiers, conspiracy, valuation hearing, joint and several restitution, civil damages, injunctive relief, and enforcement/nonseverable rulemaking (L. 1992 S.B. 498 §§ 1, 2, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Citation of gang prevention act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 578.421 to 578.437 as the Missouri Criminal Street Gangs Prevention Act.

headings.title: Definitions of gang and pattern of activity
headings.reviewNote: Defines criminal street gang and pattern of criminal street gang activity by enumerating seventeen qualifying trigger offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.421 covering the Missouri Criminal Street Gangs Prevention Act short title and definitions of criminal street gang and pattern of criminal street gang activity (L. 1993 H.B. 562 § 1 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 737 & 486).

headings.title: Labor union and concerted employee activity exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts lawful labor organizations, union agents, and concerted employee mutual aid activities from gang prevention statutes.

headings.title: Local municipal gang ordinances and nonpreemption
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes local governments to enact consistent gang ordinances, providing alternative remedies without state preemption.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.427 covering labor union and concerted employee activity exemption and local governing body nonpreemption (L. 1993 H.B. 562 § 3).

headings.title: Gang premises declared common public nuisance
headings.reviewNote: Declares any building, room, or structure used by a criminal street gang in a pattern of gang activity to be a public nuisance.

headings.title: Civil injunctions and one-year closure orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes prosecutors and the attorney general to enjoin nuisances, permitting courts to order premises closed up to one year upon owner knowledge.

headings.title: Parties defendant in nuisance abatement suits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes joining property owners, lessees, officers, agents, and facilitators as defendants in equity abatement suits.

headings.title: Criminal felony penalty for maintaining gang nuisance
headings.reviewNote: Designates maintaining a gang-related public nuisance as a class D felony punishable by indictment or information.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.430 covering gang premises public nuisance declaration, equity injunctions and up to one-year non-occupancy orders, defendant joinder, and class D felony penalty (L. 1993 H.B. 562 § 4 subsecs. 1, 2, 3, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Definition of weapon for gang confiscation
headings.reviewNote: Defines weapon for gang prevention statutes by incorporating statutory definitions of firearms, knives, explosive weapons, and prohibited items.

headings.title: Confiscation, judicial nuisance declaration, and destruction
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes peace officers to confiscate weapons possessed by gang members, initiate circuit court nuisance petitions, and obtain destruction orders.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.435 covering weapon definition by reference to section 571.010 and gang weapon confiscation, circuit court nuisance petition, and destruction (L. 1993 H.B. 562 § 5 subsecs. 1, 2).

headings.title: Conspicuous notice of client background information
headings.reviewNote: Requires international marriage brokers to provide conspicuous written notice in the recruit's native language regarding client background rights.

headings.title: Mandatory dissemination of background records to recruits
headings.reviewNote: Directs the broker to disseminate client criminal and marital history and basic rights information to a recruit within thirty days of receiving it, in the recruit's native language at the organization's translation expense.

headings.title: Client criminal and marital history obligations
headings.reviewNote: Requires a client of an international marriage broker to obtain a copy of his or her own criminal history record information and provide both criminal history and marital history information to the broker.

headings.title: Client affirmation of complete marital history
headings.reviewNote: Requires the broker to obtain the client's affirmation that marital history information is complete and accurate, including marriages, annulments, and dissolutions in other states or foreign countries.

headings.title: Suspension of services until disclosures are provided
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits an international marriage broker from providing any further services to the client or recruit until required criminal and marital history information is obtained and provided to the recruit.

headings.title: When broker is deemed doing business in Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Deems an international marriage broker to be doing business in Missouri if it contracts for matchmaking services with a Missouri resident or qualifies under other Missouri laws.

headings.title: Exemption from sexual offender registration
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a person found guilty of violating this section is not required to register as a sexual offender under section 589.400 unless otherwise required under that section.

headings.title: Class E felony for willfully providing false information
headings.reviewNote: Classifies willfully providing incomplete or false information pursuant to this section as a class E felony.

headings.title: Class E felony for failing to provide information or notice
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to provide the information and notice required pursuant to this section as a class E felony.

headings.title: Nonpreemption of other legal rights and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section preempts any other right or remedy available under law to any party using an international marriage broker or organization.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsection headings for 578.475 (rewrote fabricated subsections 3–10 and corrected subsection 2 note) covering conspicuous recruit notice, 30-day translated record dissemination, client history obligations and affirmation, service suspension, doing business in Missouri, sex offender registration exemption, class E felony penalties, and nonpreemption (L. 2005 H.B. 353, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; transferred from former 566.221; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of unlawful outdoor sporting on private land
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful fishing, hunting, or trapping on private land as fishing, hunting, trapping, or retrieving wildlife on private land not owned or possessed by the person without owner or lessee permission.

headings.title: License surrender and revocation of privileges
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to require surrender of department of conservation licenses or permits for knowing violations of subsection 1 and directs the court to notify the conservation commission of any conviction to request revocation of privileges for at least one year.

headings.title: Affirmative defense for premises open to public
headings.reviewNote: Provides an affirmative defense if the premises were open to members of the public at the time and the person complied with all lawful conditions for access or remaining.

headings.title: Penalty classification for unlawful hunting, fishing, or trapping
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful fishing, hunting, or trapping on private land as a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.520 (rewrote shifted subsections 2 through 4) covering unlawful fishing, hunting, trapping, or wildlife retrieval on private land, license surrender and privilege revocation request, open-to-public affirmative defense, and class B misdemeanor penalty (L. 2007 S.B. 198, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of unlawful retrieval of large or small game
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful retrieval of large or small game when a person retrieving wildlife on private land with landowner or lessee permission intentionally drives or flushes game toward other hunters in the same group or intentionally discharges a firearm at game originating from the land during retrieval.

headings.title: Affirmative defense for premises open to public
headings.reviewNote: Provides an affirmative defense if the premises were open to members of the public at the time and the person complied with all lawful conditions for access or remaining.

headings.title: Penalty classification for unlawful game retrieval
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful retrieval of large or small game as a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.525 (rewrote inaccurate subsections 1 and 2 and corrected subsection 3 penalty to class B misdemeanor) covering unlawful game retrieval acts while retrieving with permission, open-to-public affirmative defense, and class B misdemeanor penalty (L. 2007 S.B. 198, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Citation of large carnivore act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 578.600 to 578.624 as the Large Carnivore Act.

headings.title: Definitions of large carnivore and terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines circus, department, division, facility, humane killing, large carnivore (specified nonnative Felidae and nonnative bears), livestock, permit, and qualified veterinarian for sections 578.600 to 578.624.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.600 (tightened subsection 2 note) covering Large Carnivore Act short title and nine statutory definitions (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Prohibition against owning or breeding large carnivores
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits owning, possessing, breeding, transporting, or transferring large carnivores except in strict compliance with the Large Carnivore Act.

headings.title: Legislative purpose and public safety intent
headings.reviewNote: Declares the statutory intent to protect public health and safety and promote humane treatment of captive wild carnivores.

headings.title: Division permit requirement, contents, and fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires a division of animal health permit for each large carnivore possessed, bred, or transported on or after January 1, 2012 (with a sixty-day application window for existing holders), specifying required permit details, veterinary microchipping and DNA sampling, and maximum initial ($2,500) and annual renewal ($500) fees.

headings.title: Disqualifications for permit issuance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing a permit to any person under twenty-one years of age or who has been found guilty of or pled guilty to any state or local animal neglect or mistreatment law or, within the previous ten years, any felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 578.602 (rewrote inaccurate subsections 3 and 4) covering large carnivore prohibitions, division enforcement purposes, division permit requirements and fees, and permit disqualifications (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Mandatory compliance with federal USDA standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires any person who owns, possesses, breeds, or sells a large carnivore to adhere to all United States Department of Agriculture regulations and standards.

headings.title: Mandatory notification of department upon animal death
headings.reviewNote: Requires the owner to notify the state department of agriculture within ten business days of a large carnivore's death, including the animal's subcutaneous microchip identification number.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.606 (corrected subsection 2 notification window from 24 hours to ten business days) covering USDA regulatory compliance and ten-business-day death notification with microchip ID (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Authorization to kill escaped or threatening carnivore
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a law enforcement officer or other person to kill a large carnivore observed or reasonably believed to be chasing, attacking, injuring, or killing a human (inside or outside its enclosure), livestock, poultry, or a mammalian pet outside its enclosure.

headings.title: Immunity from civil liability
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from civil liability for damages or otherwise to any law enforcement officer, animal control officer, or person killing or attempting to kill a large carnivore under subsection 1.

headings.title: Trespass onto livestock or poultry premises and damages
headings.reviewNote: Declares a large carnivore's entry onto a field or enclosure owned or leased by a livestock or poultry producer to be a trespass and holds the owner or possessor liable in damages.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.608 (narrowed subsection 2 to civil immunity and corrected subsection 3 to livestock/poultry premises trespass) covering authority to kill threatening large carnivores, civil liability immunity, and trespass damages on livestock or poultry premises (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Civil liability for human death, injury, or property damage
headings.reviewNote: Holds any owner or possessor of a large carnivore civilly liable for human death or injury and property damage (including death or injury of another animal) without limiting common law liability.

headings.title: Mandatory liability insurance and annual verification
headings.reviewNote: Requires any owner or possessor of a large carnivore to maintain at least $250,000 in liability insurance and provide annual verification to the department.

headings.title: Mandatory emergency reporting of carnivore escapes
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate reporting to law enforcement upon intentional or unintentional escape or release of a large carnivore and holds the owner or possessor liable for all recapture expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 578.610 (refined subsection 1 and removed fabricated surety bond from subsection 2) covering civil liability for death, injury, or property damage, $250,000 liability insurance with annual verification, and immediate escape reporting with recapture cost liability (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Criminal penalties and additional sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Classifies Large Carnivore Act and permit violations as class A misdemeanors and intentional release (except to another person's care, custody, and control) as a class E felony, and authorizes up to 500 hours of community service or loss of privileges to own or possess any animal.

headings.title: Exemption for officials and veterinarians performing duties
headings.reviewNote: Exempts law enforcement officers, animal control officers, qualified veterinarians, and department of agriculture employees performing their duties under sections 578.600 to 578.624 from subsection 1 penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.614 (rewrote inaccurate subsection 1 and fabricated subsection 2) covering class A misdemeanor and intentional-release class E felony penalties with optional community service or ownership-privilege loss, and official/veterinarian duty exemption (L. 2010 S.B. 795, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Large carnivores subject to civil forfeiture
headings.reviewNote: Subjects a violator's large carnivore and any other large carnivore owned or possessed by that person to civil forfeiture upon violation of sections 578.600 to 578.624.

headings.title: Prosecuting attorney petition for civil forfeiture order
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the prosecuting attorney in an action under section 578.614 to petition the court for an order of civil forfeiture of all large carnivores owned or possessed by the violator.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.616 (rewrote inaccurate subsections 1 and 2, removing fabricated sanctuary transfer) covering civil forfeiture eligibility for large carnivores and prosecuting attorney forfeiture petitions under section 578.614 (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Exempt entities and grandfathered class C exhibitors
headings.reviewNote: Exempts from sections 578.602 and 578.604 animal control/protection shelters providing temporary care up to 90 days, law enforcement and agriculture department personnel, veterinarians in temporary possession, and qualifying 9 C.F.R. 1.1 class C licensees owning or possessing a large carnivore on August 28, 2010.

headings.title: Exemption for nonresidents in interstate transit
headings.reviewNote: Exempts from sections 578.602 and 578.604 nonresidents in Missouri solely for travel between out-of-state locations who are not exhibiting in the state.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.620 (corrected subsection 1 note to match actual exemptions from sections 578.602 and 578.604) covering temporary shelters, officials, veterinarians, grandfathered class C licensees as of August 28, 2010, and nonresidents in transit (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Large carnivore fund creation and treasury management
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Large Carnivore Fund in the state treasury, providing for interest crediting and nonreversion to general revenue under section 33.080.

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Conditions effectiveness of rules created under sections 578.600 to 578.624 on compliance with chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a nonseverability clause invalidating rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2010 if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 578.624 (tightened subsection 2 title/note) covering Large Carnivore Fund creation, treasury custody, and section 33.080 nonreversion, plus chapter 536 rulemaking effectiveness and nonseverability (L. 2010 S.B. 795).

headings.title: Application of chapter 486 notary definitions
headings.reviewNote: Applies the statutory definitions from section 486.600 to all provisions governing criminal notary misconduct.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalties for official notary misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failing to require personal presence, failing to verify identity, or executing false certificates as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for general notary violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies performing acts prohibited by chapter 486 or failing to perform required notarial duties as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalty for impersonating a notary
headings.reviewNote: Designates acting as or impersonating a commissioned notary public without authorization as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Concealing or defacing notary seal and journal
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly obtaining, concealing, defacing, or destroying a notary's official seal, journal, or records as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Coercing or influencing notary official misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Designates soliciting, coercing, or influencing a notary public to commit official misconduct as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Tampering with electronic notary security credentials
headings.reviewNote: Classifies obtaining, concealing, or destroying electronic notary signatures, encryption keys, or digital tokens as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Cumulative nature of other remedies and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory criminal penalties do not preclude civil liabilities, administrative disciplinary sanctions, or other legal remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 578.700 covering section 486.600 definitions, notary misconduct misdemeanors, general chapter 486 violations, notary impersonation, seal/journal tampering, coercing misconduct, electronic notary credential tampering, and cumulative remedies (L. 2020 H.B. 1655).
